claim.spatial_precision: widespread/systematic state and military practice documented nationally, without converting that wording into a prevalence polygon
claim.summary: The ILO Commission of Inquiry concluded in 1998 that forced or compulsory labour was imposed in Myanmar in a widespread and systematic manner, particularly by government officials and the military. The atlas records a strong positive state-forced-labour claim for 1998 while preserving the distinction between the Commission's national institutional finding and any finer-grained spatial distribution.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim 295db38e-3b6d-41b8-8563-721ec6757328 into current post-M1 semantics. No new P-level is assigned. Legacy geometry 26675f14-f67f-4ff4-a1e7-00c3ca71fc20 is an explicit modern/navigation proxy and is not promoted as this claim's historical/practice inference extent.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded classification only. Do not infer national prevalence, uniform territorial distribution, legal status, or a country-wide practice polygon beyond what the evidence directly supports.

source.title: Report of ILO Commission of Inquiry reveals widespread and systematic use of forced labour in Myanmar (Burma)
source.independence_notes: Official ILO Commission-of-Inquiry finding. News summaries and follow-up ILO statements quoting the same Commission belong to the same evidence family.
source.reliability_limitations: The Commission supports widespread/systematic state forced labour but does not provide a geometry suitable for mapping local prevalence or every affected locality.
